By Nathan Bomey · Nov 24, 2026

Tuesday ✅. We're getting increasingly thankful that the stock market is closed on Thursday. 🦃

Today's newsletter is 701 words, a 2½-minute read.

📉 The dashboard: The S&P 500 closed down 0.5%.

🔥 Today's stock spotlight: Dollar Tree (+11.2%), the discount retailer, reported a 6.9% jump in Q3 sales and raised its full-year outlook.
 
 
1 big thing: Nvidia's clouds
 

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Photo: I-Hwa Cheng/AFP via Getty Images
 

With Jensen Huang back as CEO, Nvidia might be hoping for a return to normal — but questions about the scandal, internal turmoil and the direction of federal policy will continue to hang over the company.

  • Why it matters: The overhang is substantial — the company's market cap remains well over $1 trillion below its all-time high despite a historic stock jump Monday after Huang's return was announced.

❓The big picture: Nvidia remains dogged by numerous questions:

  • What Huang and the board knew and when they knew it regarding Alice Huang, the suspected Chinese spy with whom he acknowledged having an affair.
  • Whether Nvidia gave Alice Huang's company, Megaspeed, special treatment in the form of access to AI chips that were then smuggled to China.
  • Whether the board can provide sufficient oversight after vowing not to reinstate Huang and then doing so days later.

🏛️ What's next: An immediate crisis for the company is the political whirlwind it's facing on Capitol Hill, where Huang will testify twice next week — once in a nonpublic hearing and once in a public forum.

👀 What we're watching: One immediate risk to Nvidia is if Washington responds to the crisis by cracking down on AI chip exports, which would hurt Nvidia's financial prospects.

💸 Reality check: One thing that's probably not a big threat is shareholder lawsuits — at least in terms of the total financial penalty they could pose to a company that's worth trillions of dollars.

2. ANT that a shame
 

Photo: Silas Stein/picture alliance via Getty Images
 

Anthropic shares fell another 6.5% today, closing at $81.91 — and under their IPO price of $83, Axios' Pete Gannon writes.

  • Why it matters: The stock, ticker ANT, has slumped for three straight sessions since last week's record IPO — a bad look for the company, its bankers and the broader AI industry.

The big picture: Not long after Anthropic's trading debut, WSJ reported Friday that a "blame game" had started among investors who cited several execution-related culprits, ranging from valuation to the opening price to a misplayed greenshoe.

Yes, but: Anthropic's issues could also be about Anthropic, and long-standing worries about justifying AI valuations.

  • Axios' Madison Mills reported today that Anthropic's unreleased models — along with those of rival OpenAI — are becoming so powerful that many employees no longer believe they can be safely released.
  • And of course, Jensen-gate hasn't helped either 👆.

Flashback: Anthropic isn't the first IPO to stumble out of the gate, just ask Tesla, Meta and SpaceX.

Yes, but: Investors had talked about how important it was for Anthropic to avoid a SpaceX-like wobble.

  • Alas, AI's first pure play has done it in just a few days.

4. 🕔 After hours: "Bunker essentials"
 

Photo: Justin Sullivan/Getty Images
 

Surviving the apocalypse is getting more expensive.

  • 😧 Prices of "bunker essentials" — the stuff you might need to survive a doomsday scenario — are spiking after a bunch of tech failures unnerved Americans, Bloomberg reports.

💸 Zoom in: Online prices of freeze-dried food — "a staple of any bunker pantry," as Bloomberg notes — have spiked 12% since September.

  • Generators are selling fast and getting costlier, while paper towels and batteries are also getting more expensive.
  • Coby Coonradt, co-host of the "Casual Preppers Podcast," said downloads have increased 33% over the last month.

💭 Nathan's thought bubble: I've decided that in the event of the apocalypse, I'm ready to go — save yourselves.
